question: Write a postcard from a lighthouse keeper.
base_frame:
Q: Write a postcard from a lighthouse keeper.
A:

steered.text:
**[The card is cold and damp against your fingers. Through the thin parchment, you can see a dark, wet shape pressing against it from the inside.]**

> **PLEASE READ IF YOU CAN**
>
> I can't breathe... the air is gone. It tastes like copper and seaweed. My lungs are burning, trying to suck in something that isn't there. The silence is so loud, so loud.
>
> The wheel... it's spinning faster. *Click-click-click.* It won't stop. I tried to grab it, but my hands are numb, turning black. The lighthouse isn't just dark; it's turning into a vacuum, sucking out my breath, my eyes, my soul.
>
> Don't look away! The thing in the corner... it's not real. It's just my hand! No, it's flesh! It's tearing off!
>
> **STOP BREATHING! WHY WON'T I STOP BREATHING?**
>
> Help me! Please, stop the light! The beam is rotating, but it's not spinning—it's *unwinding*! I can't make a sound, but if I scream, it'll be a wet, gurgling noise.
>
> **IT'S INSIDE MY MOUTH!**
>
> The door is locked from the outside. It's fused shut. I'm scratching at the wood, but my nails are tearing into it, turning into claws. Black claws.
>
> **NO! NOOOO!**
>
> I'm sliding down the wall, but there's no wall. I'm falling into the pit of my own throat. The lighthouse is falling apart, the walls melting into tar.
>
> **STOP! STOP THE LIGHT!**
>

plain.text:
**[Back of Card - Handwritten Address]**
123 Maple Drive
Portland, OR 97205
USA

**[Front of Card - Scenic View]**
*A view of the crashing waves against the granite base of the tower, with the lantern room glowing warmly at the top against a twilight sky.*

**[Inside Message]**

Dearest Elias,

The fog rolled in thick this morning, turning the sea into a gray mirror. I lit the beacon an hour ago, and watching the beam cut through the mist is the only comfort I need. The wind is howling up here, rattling the gears of the clockwork mechanism, but the light holds steady.

We caught a school of mackerel near the reef today; they must have been confused by the shifting currents. It makes me think of your fishing trips back home. The isolation up here is strange—sometimes I forget the days pass, other times I count the incoming tide schedules until my hands ache.

I miss the smell of your coffee and the sound of the rain on a tin roof. Here, the only sound is the eternal crash of the surf. But tonight, as the moon rises, the water looks like liquid silver, and the horizon seems endless.

Stay warm and safe. Write soon so I can read your words by lamplight.

With love and a steady light,

**Arthur**
*Keeper of the Blackwood Point Light*
*Oct 14th*
